 These Miscellaneous First Appeals, Coming On
For Orders This Day, Umesh M. Adiga. J., Delivered
The Following:
 Judgment

Insurer as well as claimants in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 have filed appeals in M.F.A.No.201561 of 2019 and M.F.A. No.200313 of 2020, challenging the judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Basavana Bagewadi (for short, the Tribunal) in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 dated 21.02.2019.

The Insurer has challenged its liability to pay compensation, so also,
quantum of the compensation.
The claimants filed the appeal challenging the judgment for enhancement of the compensation.

2. It is the case of claimants/petitioners that on 28.01.2015, deceased Kashinath Pawar, Son of Bhoju Pawar, who was traveling in the official Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03/MP-4483 from Vijayapura towards Bengaluru, at about 11.30 pm., when the said Car reached near Shira, a lorry was going ahead of the Car in the place of the accident, which was bearing Reg.No.TN-77/Y-0408.
The NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB driver of the said lorry was driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and he suddenly applied the brake without giving nay signal.
Due to which, driver of the Car could not control his vehicle and dashed against back side of the lorry.
It appears, after the accident, the lorry dragged the Car to an extent of 150 meters ahead.
Due to impact, driver of the Car as well as Kashinath Pawar had sustained grievous injuries and the said Kashinath succumbed to the injuries.
3. It is the further case of the claimants that deceased was aged 39 years.

He was Senior KAS Officer in Government of Karnataka and as on the date of the accident, he was serving as Chief Administrative Officer to the Banjara Development Authority and drawing salary of Rs.65,943/-
p.m., plus allowances.
Claimants are his wife and minor children, who were depending upon his earnings.
With these reasons, prayed to award compensation of Rs.1,36,23,160/-.

4. Respondent No.2/Insurer of the said lorry denied the contents of claim petition and it has stated that accident NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver; driver of the lorry was not responsible for the accident and liability of Respondent No.2 was restricted to terms and conditions of policy of the insurance and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5.

Respondent Nos.3 and 4 have denied contents of the petition and they have further contended that accident was not caused due to negligence of the driver of the Car and the said Car was duly insured with Respondent No.4 and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. The Tribunal had framed necessary issues.

Respondent examined RW-1 and got marked Ex.R1.
8.

The Tribunal, after hearing both sides and on appreciating pleadings and evidence on record, by the impugned judgment awarded following compensation:
 Sl.

No . Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 89,26,965  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB  2. Loss of love and affection 40,000  3. Funeral expenses 15,000  4. Transportation of dead body 10,000  5. Loss of consortium/Estate 15,000  Total 90,06,965  9.

The Tribunal has apportioned the liability between Respondent Nos.2 an 4 in the ratio of 80% : 20%.
10.
We have heard the arguments.

11. The learned advocate for the Insurer has submitted that looking to the prosecution papers,
accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the Car by its driver and driver of the lorry was not at all responsible for the accident and at the most, his responsibility might be 10 to 20%, because the Car dashed against back side of lorry and Car was in the high speed, because of which, the Car itself dragged the lorry to an extent of 150 meters, which indicates the speed of the Car.
She has further submitted that the driver of the Car did not keep proper distance between lorry and the Car at the time of the accident.
Therefore, it is the liability of Respondent No.4 to pay the entire amount of compensation.
The learned advocate for the Insurer has also submitted that the Tribunal has awarded higher compensation under other heads.
Therefore, prayed to modulate the amount of compensation.

13. The learned advocate for claimants submitted that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence and came to a right conclusion that accident was taken due to contributory negligence of the driver of the lorry and the Car.

The contribution of the driver of the lorry is much more than the Smt. Jayashree W/O Kashinath Pawar And ... vs Sri Selvam P S/O Perumal And Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96079341/
6 driver of the Car.
Therefore, the Tribunal has apportioned negligence in the ratio of 80 : 20 and it does not call for any interference.
14. The learned counsel further submitted that the Tribunal has not taken future prospects at the rate of 50% though the deceased was aged about 40 years at the time of the accident.
The Tribunal has not awarded just compensation on other heads.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the same.

The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in apportioning the liability in the ratio of 80 : 20 between the Lorry and the Car?
ii) Whether the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs to be re-visited?
16. The accident is not in dispute and death of Kashinath in vehicle accident also is not in dispute.
The dispute of Insurer is that, maximum contributory negligence was of driver of the Car.

However,
the Tribunal has erroneously held that the contributory negligence of the driver of the lorry was 80%, which needs to be corrected.
17. The learned advocate for Respondent No.4 contends that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence and came to right conclusion.
It is not in dispute that both Car and Lorry were going in the same direction, i.e., from Shira towards Bengaluru.
The manner in which the accident had taken place is also not in dispute.
The prosecution papers reveal that the Car dashed to the back side of the lorry and struck at back and dragged to an extent - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB of 150 meters.
This fact is mentioned in Exs.P1 and P2.
Claimants examined PW-2, who is an eye-witness.
The learned advocate for Respondent No.2 (Insurer) has suggested to PW-2 that after accident, the lorry dragged the Car to an extent of 150 meters.
Considering the evidence of PW-2 and also the prosecution papers, it can be safely believed that accident was taken place due to equal contributions of drivers of both the vehicles.
18. As per the case of the claimants, the driver of the lorry suddenly applied the brake, because of which, the Car banged the lorry from its back side and struck below the chassis.
Thereafter, both the vehicles went ahead upto 150 meters.

For sake of discussion, if accident had taken place as contended by claimants and if driver of the lorry suddenly applied the brake and stopped the vehicle, then the driver of the lorry dragging the Car does not arise.

The suggestion of Respondent No.2 to PW-2 that due to the speed of the Car, the lorry was dragged ahead to an extent of 150 Smt. Jayashree W/O Kashinath Pawar And ... vs Sri Selvam P S/O Perumal And Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96079341/
7 meters, cannot be ruled out.

sentences.text:
It is also pertinent to note that the Insurer of the lorry did not accept that driver of the lorry,
suddenly applied the brake.
Therefore, the evidence of PW-2 that the driver of the lorry was negligent and after the accident, dragged the Car to an extent of 150 meters is also cannot be ignored.
Therefore, the contributory negligence for causing the accident by driver of both the vehicles is equal.

Hence, the apportionment of contributory negligence for causing the accident is in the ratio of 50 : 50.
20.
The deceased was a Senior KAS officer, is not in dispute.
As rightly submitted by the learned advocate for the Insurer, claimants have not placed on record, better evidence, to prove the annual income of the deceased.

There was no hurdle for the claimants to produce Form No.16 or Income-tax returns to prove annual income and income-tax paid by deceased to assist the Tribunal to assess exact income of the deceased, income-tax or other tax paid by him.
For the reasons best known to the claimants, they did not place reliable materials on record; And forced the Tribunal to assess the same by guess work.
Therefore, the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB Tribunal has taken age of the deceased as 40 years and added 30% of his income towards future prospects.

21. In this appeal, claimants have placed Xerox copy of the Aadhar Card, Study Certificate,
Verification Certificate, etc., which indicates the date of birth of the deceased, Kashinath as 14.01.1975.
The date of accident is 28.01.2015.
As on the date of accident, he had completed 40 years and 13 days.

The learned advocate for the Insurer has submitted that since he crossed the age of 40 years, the future prospects cannot be taken as 50% and the Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing the future prospects as 30%.
On the contrary, the learned advocate for the claimants has submitted that motor vehicle compensation provision is benevolent legislation.
Strict rule of law is not applicable.
As on the date of accident, deceased just completed age of 40 years and hardly, about 12 to 13 days above the age of 40 years.
Hence, benefit of addition of 50% cannot be denied because of 12 to 13 days.
He further submitted that the deceased left behind him his widow and - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB two minor children.
The sole earning member of the family has died.
Therefore, the Court has to take lenient view to award just compensation to the claimants.

sentences.text: The submission of the learned advocate for the claimants is acceptable.

It is true that in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1 and also in the case of SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION2, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that when the deceased or victim of an accident is a Government Servant, or having fixed salary and his age is upto 40 years, future prospects has to be considered to an extent of 50%.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case,
admittedly, he was aged about 40 years and hardly about 13 days above 40 years.
Under these circumstances, addition of future prospects has to be taken at the rate of 50% and not 30% as taken by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses and applied multipliers as '15'.
As per Ex.P7, the total salary drawn by the deceased was Rs.65,943/- per month.
Ex.P7 shows that Rs.200/- was deducted from his salary towards professional tax.
How much income-tax deceased had paid to Income- tax Department is not disclosed by proper records.
Therefore, the Court has to take judicial notice.
During the year 2015, tax exemption limit was up to Rs.2,50,000/-.
Thereafter, upto Rs.5,00,000/- rate of income-tax was 10%.
The total income of the deceased per annum is Rs.7,91,316/- and after deduction of income-tax and professional tax of Rs.56,531/-, his net income was Rs.7,34,785/-.

50% of the said income has to be added towards future prospects,
which is Rs.3,67,392/- and 1/3rd of the said aggregate has to be deducted towards personal expenses, which is again Rs.3,67,392/-.
Therefore, the net income on which, the members of the family might be depending was (Rs.7,34,785 X 15) = Rs.1,10,21,775/-.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.1,10,21,775/-.
As held in the case of PRANAY SETHI and SARLA VERMA (referred supra), Rs.40,000/- shall be awarded to each claimants for loss of consortium.
And Rs.15,000/-each under the head loss of estate and funeral expenses.

The claimants are entitled for the following amount of compensation:
 Sl.No. Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 1,10,21,775  2. Loss of consortium 1,20,000
3 . Funeral expenses 15,000
4. Loss of estate 15,000  Total 1,11,71,775

For the aforesaid reasons, we answer Point No.1 in the negative and Point No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The Appeals in M.F.A.No.201561 of 2019 and M.F.A.No.200313 of 2020 are partly allowed.

The impugned judgment and award dated 21.02.2019 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT IX, Basavana Bagewadi in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 is modified as under:
a) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,11,71,775/- (Rupees One Crore Eleven Lakhs Seventy One Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy Five only) as against Rs.90,06,965/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,64,810/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Eight Hundred and Ten only) with interest at the rate of 6% on the enhanced amount, from the date of petition, till its payment, excluding delayed period of 872 days in filing appeal, by the claimants.
b) The Appellant/Insurer of the lorry and Respondent No.4/Insurer of the Car shall - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB deposit the said amount in the ratio of 50 : 50, within a period of eight weeks, from the date of receipt of copy of the award.
The orders passed by the Tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release of the amount are not disturbed.

The Following:
 Judgment
Insurer as well as claimants in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 have filed appeals in M.F.A.No.201561 of 2019 and M.F.A. No.200313 of 2020, challenging the judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Basavana Bagewadi (for short, the Tribunal) in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 dated 21.02.2019.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Insurer has challenged its liability to pay compensation, so also,
quantum of the compensation.
Due to impact, driver of the Car as well as Kashinath Pawar had sustained grievous injuries and the said Kashinath succumbed to the injuries.
He was Senior KAS Officer in Government of Karnataka and as on the date of the accident, he was serving as Chief Administrative Officer to the Banjara Development Authority and drawing salary of Rs.65,943/-
p.m., plus allowances.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Tribunal has not awarded just compensation on other heads.
17. The learned advocate for Respondent No.4 contends that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence and came to right conclusion.
The learned advocate for the Insurer has submitted that since he crossed the age of 40 years, the future prospects cannot be taken as 50% and the Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing the future prospects as 30%.
On the contrary, the learned advocate for the claimants has submitted that motor vehicle compensation provision is benevolent legislation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in apportioning the liability in the ratio of 80 : 20 between the Lorry and the Car?
ii) Whether the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs to be re-visited?
16. The accident is not in dispute and death of Kashinath in vehicle accident also is not in dispute.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However,
the Tribunal has erroneously held that the contributory negligence of the driver of the lorry was 80%, which needs to be corrected.
Considering the evidence of PW-2 and also the prosecution papers, it can be safely believed that accident was taken place due to equal contributions of drivers of both the vehicles.
Therefore, the contributory negligence for causing the accident by driver of both the vehicles is equal.
The deceased was a Senior KAS officer, is not in dispute.
There was no hurdle for the claimants to produce Form No.16 or Income-tax returns to prove annual income and income-tax paid by deceased to assist the Tribunal to assess exact income of the deceased, income-tax or other tax paid by him.
For the reasons best known to the claimants, they did not place reliable materials on record; And forced the Tribunal to assess the same by guess work.
As on the date of accident, he had completed 40 years and 13 days.
Strict rule of law is not applicable.
As on the date of accident, deceased just completed age of 40 years and hardly, about 12 to 13 days above the age of 40 years.
Hence, benefit of addition of 50% cannot be denied because of 12 to 13 days.
He further submitted that the deceased left behind him his widow and - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB two minor children.
The sole earning member of the family has died.
Therefore, the Court has to take lenient view to award just compensation to the claimants.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the Court has to take judicial notice.
During the year 2015, tax exemption limit was up to Rs.2,50,000/-.
Thereafter, upto Rs.5,00,000/- rate of income-tax was 10%.
The total income of the deceased per annum is Rs.7,91,316/- and after deduction of income-tax and professional tax of Rs.56,531/-, his net income was Rs.7,34,785/-.
50% of the said income has to be added towards future prospects,
which is Rs.3,67,392/- and 1/3rd of the said aggregate has to be deducted towards personal expenses, which is again Rs.3,67,392/-.
Therefore, the net income on which, the members of the family might be depending was (Rs.7,34,785 X 15) = Rs.1,10,21,775/-.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.1,10,21,775/-.
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB 24.
As held in the case of PRANAY SETHI and SARLA VERMA (referred supra), Rs.40,000/- shall be awarded to each claimants for loss of consortium.
And Rs.15,000/-each under the head loss of estate and funeral expenses.
The claimants are entitled for the following amount of compensation:
 Sl.No. Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 1,10,21,775  2. Loss of consortium 1,20,000
3 . Funeral expenses 15,000
4. Loss of estate 15,000  Total 1,11,71,775
The claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation of (Rs.1,11,71,775-Rs.90,06,965) =
Rs.21,64,810/-.
25.
Respondent Nos.1 and 4, i.e., Insurer of the lorry and Insurer of the Car are equally liable to pay the said amount, i.e., in the ratio of 50 : 50.
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB 26.
For the aforesaid reasons, we answer Point No.1 in the negative and Point No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The Appeals in M.F.A.No.201561 of 2019 and M.F.A.No.200313 of 2020 are partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award dated 21.02.2019 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT IX, Basavana Bagewadi in M.V.C.No.1287 of 2015 is modified as under:
a) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,11,71,775/- (Rupees One Crore Eleven Lakhs Seventy One Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy Five only) as against Rs.90,06,965/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,64,810/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Eight Hundred and Ten only) with interest at the rate of 6% on the enhanced amount, from the date of petition, till its payment, excluding delayed period of 872 days in filing appeal, by the claimants.
b) The Appellant/Insurer of the lorry and Respondent No.4/Insurer of the Car shall - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5704-DB deposit the said amount in the ratio of 50 : 50, within a period of eight weeks, from the date of receipt of copy of the award.
The orders passed by the Tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release of the amount are not disturbed.
